$comment: The provider CLI releases the approval contract is tested against.
Pinned rather than resolved from `latest` at run time, because a red
compatibility run has to name a version somebody can install and reproduce.
A release enters this matrix through a reviewed change to this file, and
leaves it the same way -- `.github/workflows/cli-versions.yml` opens an
issue when npm's newest three differ from what is pinned here, and never
edits the list itself. Dropping an older version silently is the failure
mode that matters: it turns 'we stopped testing that' into a diff nobody
Newest first. `policy.versions` is how many releases of each CLI the
matrix is meant to cover, and a provider that pins any other number fails
both the per-PR test in tests/test_cli_compatibility.py and the `pinned`
job in cli-compatibility.yml -- so a matrix that has quietly shrunk is a
red X on the commit that shrank it, rather than a smaller test run.
